thought.text: Unauthenticated API access to the public project works! The issue is the placeholder token `glpat-XXX` (invalid). Let me check how the gitlab client handles empty tokens:

reasoning_content:
Interesting — this app's `GetFile` calls the GitLab API using `ref` from the raw URL (main). When the token is `glpat-XXX` (invalid), it returns 401 Unauthorized. But when there's no token or an empty token... wait, `curl` without a token succeeded in fetching the file! The project seems to be public, and the API allows unauthenticated file reads.

But when I tested with `-H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: "`, a 400 was returned saying "ref is missing, ref is empty" — this is just because I didn't pass the `ref` parameter in my curl. The app is passing `ref=main`.

In other words: unauthenticated API access to public projects works. The question is whether the gitlab client is built with an empty token, and whether the client sends an empty PRIVATE-TOKEN header.

Let me check how the gitlab client is constructed when `tokenFile` is empty. Looking at config.go, if `client.TokenFile != ""`, it reads the file, otherwise it uses `b = []byte{}`. The `gitlab.NewGitlabClient(baseURL, string(b), rateLimiter)` function with an empty token.

Let me check how NewGitlabClient handles an empty token.

action.command: grep -rn "NewGitlabClient" pkg/gitclient/*.go | grep -v _test | head -3; sed -n "$(grep -n 'func NewGitlabClient' pkg/gitclient/gitlab.go | cut -d: -f1),+40p" pkg/gitclient/gitlab.go
